chords._schema: strings ordered low E (6) to high e (1). frets: null = muted/not played, 0 = open. fingers: 0 = open, 1 = index, 2 = middle, 3 = ring, 4 = pinky, null = muted.

exercises.name: The up-strum
exercises.purpose: Light upward brush, mute on contact.

params.action: down on beat, up on the "and"
params.cue: up-strum touches only the thin strings

exercises.coaching: An up-strum is a light upward brush — mostly the thin strings, slightly muted. Down on the beat, up on the "and." Feels like a windshield wiper.

exercises.name: D-DU-UDU

params.pattern: D (1) - DU (2) - UDU (3&4) per 2-beat feel; full: D D-U U-D-U

exercises.coaching: The pattern: down, down-up, up-down-up. Over G-D-Em-C. Count it out loud. This is the strum 90% of campfire songs use.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: Down-strums got you started. Up-strums make it move. Today: the D-DU-UDU pattern — the backbone of popular strumming.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex1_intro: Up-strum: light upward brush, mostly thin strings, slightly muted. Down on the beat, up on the "and." Like a windshield wiper.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex2_intro: Pattern: down, down-up, up-down-up. Over the G-D-Em-C loop. Count 1-2-3-4. That groove is what makes people dance.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: If you can hold D-DU-UDU over the loop, your strumming sounds like songs on the radio. Big leap.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: Up-strums in. D-DU-UDU under your belt. Lesson 12 we build a small library of patterns.
